key_insight: Spatially patterned spin rotations control the imaginary-time Mpemba effect by redistributing spectral weight away from slow modes while preserving initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes.
engineering_relevance: Twist-designed initial states offer a route to faster quantum ground-state preparation by selectively avoiding slowly decaying excitations.
method: Apply spatially modulated local rotations to tune initial-state spectral weights.
Use compact-boson theory to identify mode selection and derive exact crossing times.
Test interacting XXZ chains and ladders and simulate variational imaginary-time evolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation in interacting XXZ systems and a twelve-qubit variational simulation reproducing relaxation reversals and their controlled delay.
watch_item: Hardware robustness and scaling beyond the twelve-qubit simulation remain to be established.
paper_title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
